title: Resolved: MasterCard outage left thousands of shoppers stranded
full_text:
Shoppers across Sydney and other major Australian cities were left scrambling on Saturday afternoon after a global MasterCard outage disrupted tap-and-go payments at supermarkets, cafes and retail outlets nationwide.
Reports of failed transactions began flooding social media on Saturday afternoon, with outage tracking service DownDetector recording a sharp spike in complaints just before 2pm from customers unable to complete purchases using contactless payment methods, including digital wallets on both iPhone and Android devices.
At its peak, around 3:30pm, more than 2 thousand customers reported being impacted on DownDetector’s site.
Retailers reported a surge in declined transactions during the busy Saturday trading period.
The MasterCard provider said in a statement: “A scheduled system update caused MasterCard transactions to be declined for a period of time earlier today.”
“The situation has been resolved and all systems are working as normal.”
Major Australian banks, including Westpac, Bankwest and Macquarie, moved quickly to reassure customers and offer a workaround during the outage.
The Commonwealth Bank advised affected customers to insert their physical card at the terminal and select “savings” to process payments via eftpos rather than relying on MasterCard’s network.
Westpac and ANZ also acknowledged the outage, with both banks working to manage customer inquiries as the issue unfolded.
Businesses had to turn away some blindsided customers during the outage, including Chargrill Charlie’s in Sydney, according to NewsWire.
Despite the disruption to tap-and-go and digital wallet payments, physical debit and credit cards continued to function largely as normal, and ATM services across the country remained largely unaffected, offering some relief to consumers seeking to withdraw cash as an alternative during the outage window.
